resources.name: The Animation Workshop
resources.evidence: VIA's official page names student productions including The Saga of Biorn and describes its animation education. This is a showcase, not a step-by-step tutorial.
resources.objective: Explain a visual storytelling choice before planning an original shot.
resources.practice: Choose one work from the publisher's showcase. Record its title and creator credits, then describe a staging or composition choice with a specific visual reference. Draw three original storyboard panels communicating a different action.
resources.access: External showcase; select accessible material. Viewing and media accessibility were not independently tested.

resources.name: School of Motion
resources.material: Animation Principle: Master Natural Movements with Follow Through
resources.level: Beginner to intermediate; basic After Effects familiarity
resources.evidence: Publisher article explicitly teaches follow-through in After Effects and credits Jacob Richardson and Ryan Plummer.
resources.objective: Demonstrate follow-through in a short original animation.
resources.practice: Animate an original shape or character stopping while a secondary part continues moving. Keep a before-and-after comparison and explain one timing revision.
resources.access: Public article; After Effects is commercial software. Written explanation is available; video playback and captions not tested.

resources.name: Purple Pie Studios
resources.material: Illustration lesson in the Explainer Animation Course for Beginners (descriptive label)
resources.evidence: Indexed YouTube publisher metadata identifies Purple Pie Studios and describes the second course video as creating illustrations for an explainer. Full playback could not be verified.
resources.objective: Prepare an original illustration for an explainer storyboard.
resources.practice: Create an original three-panel explainer and document which illustration elements would move independently.
resources.access: User confirmed this link works on 8 November 2026. Playback was not independently tested.

resources.name: CG Cookie
resources.material: BLENDER BASICS: An Introduction to Blender 3D 4.5 LTS
resources.evidence: Publisher identifies a free 30-lesson course by Paul Caggegi covering navigation, modeling, lighting, rendering and animation. Page title and current version text differ; check the version lesson before starting.
resources.objective: Create and document a simple original Blender asset.
resources.practice: Use the navigation and modeling sections to make an original prop from basic shapes. Save the editable project and one still render. Explain how a modeling choice supports its intended use.
resources.access: Free publisher account required; no credit card advertised. Blender version guidance may change. Enrollment and full playback not tested.

resources.name: Royal Skies LLC / Royal Skies
resources.level: Beginner to intermediate; Loptr Lab placement
resources.evidence: Indexed YouTube metadata identifies Royal Skies, and the watch-page title identifies interpolation in Blender 2.83. This verifies a different subject from the collection's cinematic-storytelling description; that description is not adopted as verified.
resources.objective: Compare interpolation choices in a short motion study.
resources.practice: Compare two interpolation settings on an original moving object and explain their effect on timing.
resources.access: Older Blender interface; full video content and current-version compatibility not verified. User confirmed access on 8 November 2026.

resources.name: CartoonSmart
resources.material: Adobe Animate Video Tutorials – Animation Lessons
resources.level: Beginner to intermediate; Loptr Lab placement
resources.evidence: Publisher page identifies free animation tutorials using Adobe Animate or Flash. Other catalog material includes paid products; free viewing is not a license to redistribute files.
resources.objective: Plan and create an original animated game-art element.
resources.practice: Choose an accessible lesson on the linked publisher page and record its exact title. Create an original animated game-art element or, if software is unavailable, a labeled frame sequence. Explain its intended visual message and one revision.
resources.access: Adobe Animate/Flash examples can be legacy. Check the selected lesson's software and access requirements; catalog listing verified, individual playback not tested.

resources.name: Video Copilot
resources.evidence: Official Basic Training index lists Keying & Transparency, Motion Tracking, Animation and Rendering. Publisher describes legacy After Effects versions; modern interface equivalence is not promised.
resources.objective: Explain and test transparency in an original composite.
resources.practice: Use your own footage or original shapes to combine a foreground and background. Save a before-and-after view and identify one edge or transparency issue to revise. A labeled still breakdown is an alternative when software is unavailable.
criteria: Visual and Audio/Sound Design and Aesthetics
resources.access: Public legacy training; After Effects is commercial. Video playback and current-version compatibility not tested.

resources.name: Film Riot
resources.material: How to Create the Vintage Film Aesthetic in After Effects | @filmriot x Adobe Video
resources.level: Beginner to intermediate; Loptr Lab placement
resources.evidence: Indexed Adobe Video tutorial metadata credits Ryan Connolly of Film Riot and describes approaches to film texture, including built-in After Effects controls. Full playback could not be verified.
resources.objective: Explain how a finishing choice changes the intended tone of a shot.
resources.practice: Compare a clean original shot with a film-texture treatment, recording why the treatment supports its intended communication.
criteria: Visual and Audio/Sound Design and Aesthetics
resources.access: Co-produced Film Riot/Adobe material. User confirmed access on 8 November 2026.

resources.name: Corridor Crew
resources.material: VFX Artists React to Bad & Great CGi 221
resources.evidence: Indexed YouTube metadata names Corridor Crew and the episode. This is commentary/breakdown material, not evidence of a complete compositing course. Full playback could not be verified.
resources.objective: Distinguish an observed image-quality issue from a hypothesis about its production.
resources.practice: Record a timestamped observation, separate it from an inference, and plan an original still-image experiment to investigate the issue.
resources.access: User confirmed access on 8 November 2026; full episode content not independently reviewed. Do not download or republish film excerpts.

resources.name: VFXstudy
resources.material: Free Beginner Course – Fusion in DaVinci Resolve
resources.level: Beginner in Fusion; basic Resolve familiarity
resources.evidence: Publisher describes a 50-second opening-sequence course using Edit and Fusion pages, including 2D/3D tools. Requires basic Media Pool, Edit and Delivery familiarity.
resources.objective: Document a simple node-based compositing workflow.
resources.practice: Following the introductory workflow, create an original short title composition or a labeled node diagram. Explain the role of each operation and revise one unclear step after review.
resources.access: Free course registration/checkout flow is shown. Do not assume account-free access. Enrollment, full playback and captions not tested.

resources.name: vfx world
resources.evidence: Indexed YouTube description links @vfxworldrsb and describes a Blender Cycles scene with a Sketchfab model. Creator-linked Gumroad also identifies @vfxworldrsb. Do not confuse this channel with unrelated VFX World domains.
resources.objective: Explain lighting and source-asset provenance in a scene.
resources.practice: Light an original scene and document each external asset's license. Use original geometry unless third-party reuse rights are verified.
criteria: Visual and Audio/Sound Design and Aesthetics
resources.access: User confirmed access on 8 November 2026; full lesson content not independently reviewed. Sketchfab availability does not establish reuse rights.

resources.name: Maxon Red Giant
resources.material: Getting Started with Universe Color Mosaic
resources.level: Beginner to intermediate; Loptr Lab placement
resources.evidence: Maxon's Cineversity identifies this tutorial and includes Red Giant/Universe learning categories. Specific video playback and lesson internals were not verified.
resources.objective: Evaluate whether a mosaic treatment supports an intended visual message.
resources.practice: Compare an original still with and without a mosaic treatment and explain how the effect changes readability and tone.
criteria: Visual and Audio/Sound Design and Aesthetics
resources.access: Commercial plugin/host requirements must be checked before purchase. User confirmed access on 8 November 2026; full lesson content not independently reviewed.
